deepdive.sec: Branded Residential Real Estate / MMR Redevelopment

bull_bear.body: Strict debt discipline (max 1:1 D/E, currently 0.6x). Internal accruals (INR 600-650 cr/year from Thane + early JDA cash) reinvested into approval costs for new pipeline. No dividend commentary; focus on balance sheet growth and funding organic pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on JDA timelines (partner dependencies can delay launches from 9 months to 2.5 years). Intense competition in Thane capping price realization. Prolonged construction cost inflation. Regulatory/approval delays in MMR. Negative operating cash flows during expansion phase.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and validated; emphasizes 'discipline' in deal-making despite market overheating. Transparent on margin mechanics (blended vs. project-level) and cash flow dynamics. Patient on valuation rerating, expecting consistency over 6-8 quarters to build institutional faith.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Achieved 50:50 legacy-vs-JDA booking mix one year ahead of 2027 target. Thane sales volume is structurally capped by micro-market saturation rather than company-specific issues, making JDA expansion critical for >20% growth. Revenue recognition follows percentage-of-completion, smoothing lumpiness seen in peers using completed-contract method.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The capital profile slide states an Avg. ROE of 24% and an FY26 Debt/Equity of 0.6, captioned "Profitable growth delivered with financial discipline."
- Growth is asset-light on the second engine — expansion into MMR is via JDAs rather than land purchase, with the first JDA signed in 2023 and ₹27,000 Cr of JDA GDV assembled since.
- The deck gives no dividend policy, buyback, payout ratio or land-acquisition budget.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Trusted, century-old Raymond Group brand heritage carried into a pure-play, independently listed real estate platform
- Capital-efficient development model combining owned land (100-acre Thane land bank) with an asset-light JDA model, enabling scalable growth while limiting land-acquisition risk
- Ranked among the top 5 listed real estate developers in MMR and top 10 listed developers in India
- Strong execution capabilities, robust quality assurance processes and technology-enabled operations supporting timely project delivery and customer engagement
- Diversified portfolio across four key MMR micro-markets (Thane, BKC, Wadala, Sion) reducing single-market concentration
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory approval delays — Delays in obtaining statutory approvals, permits and clearances may affect project launch schedules and construction timelines.
- Rising construction costs — Inflation in raw materials, labour and contracting costs may exert pressure on project margins if not managed efficiently.
- Intense market competition — Strong competition from established regional and national developers in key urban MMR micro-markets may impact pricing and market share.
- Demand sensitivity to interest rates — Changes in home loan interest rates may affect buyer affordability and influence residential sales momentum.
- Geopolitical uncertainty and cost inflation — Prolonged geopolitical tensions may lead to volatility in commodity and energy prices, resulting in higher construction material costs and potential pressure on project development economics.
- Geographic concentration in MMR — The Company's entire portfolio and 100% of turnover are concentrated within a single state (Maharashtra) and, within it, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, with nil export/international revenue — leaving performance highly exposed to a single regional real estate cycle.
- Single-segment (real estate) revenue concentration — 100% of turnover derives from construction and development of residential and retail real estate, per the BRSR business-activities disclosure — leaving the Company with no diversification away from real estate-cycle risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Thane (Legacy Land): ~45% of operations; stable pre-sales INR 1,300-1,500 cr/year; intense competition limits pricing power. JDA/MMR Expansion: ~55% of operations; high-growth engine penetrating Bandra, BKC, Wadala, Sion, Kandivali. Retail: Small but consistent value-accretive component (e.g., Park Street).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "With a 100-year umbrella brand legacy, Raymond Realty has rapidly evolved from one location to a full scale Real Estate business" — foray into real estate framed from 1925, maiden project TenX Habitat in Thane launched 2019.
- Twin Engine GDV structure: Engine 1 (own land) ₹25,000 Cr and Engine 2 (JDAs) ₹27,000 Cr, for a deck-stated total of ₹52,000 Cr.
- Own-land engine is Thane-centric ("scaled across multiple projects worth ₹ 25,000 Cr GDV in Thane"); JDA engine began with the first JDA in 2023 — The Address by GS, Bandra — and has "scaled across multiple JDA projects worth ₹27,000 Cr GDV in MMR".
- Execution credential claimed: 2022 "Accomplished a first in kind real estate milestone by delivering 3 towers, two years ahead of RERA timelines."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] 2025: "Demerged into an Independent Listed Entity" — Raymond Realty Limited, CIN L41000MH2019PLC332934, ISIN INE1SY401010, NSE symbol RAYMONDREL / BSE scrip 544420, registered office Jekegram, Pokhran Road No.1, Thane (W).
- [Naming] The covering letter signs off "For Raymond Realty Limited (formerly known as Raymond Lifestyle Limited)" — the deck offers no further explanation of the name change.
- [Leadership] Chairman Gautam Hari Singhania (has led Raymond for over 35 years); Managing Director Harmohan Sahni, a Chartered Accountant with over 30 years in real estate and core sectors; CFO Ankur Jindal, a Chartered Accountant with over 24 years' experience.
- [Booking reversal] Invictus by GS (BKC) shows negative Q1FY27 activity — No of Bookings (1) and Value of Bookings -6 Cr — implying a cancellation, which the deck does not comment on.
- [Disclaimer] The deck states the information "has not been subjected to review by Auditors or the Board of Directors of the Company" and that prior-period figures have been regrouped/reclassified.

It caters to individual homebuyers and investors seeking premium residential and commercial/retail properties in MMR micro-markets including Thane, Bandra, BKC, Wadala and Sion.

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Blended EBITDA margin guided at 16-18% for FY27. New launches start with single-digit margins, maturing to ~20%+; portfolio mix drives blended rate. Construction cost inflation (war/commodity) estimated at 3-4% impact if prolonged, but fully pass-through expected; no margin erosion anticipated. Ceramic supply disruptions (Morbi) deemed non-material.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: >20% YoY (minimum guidance). EBITDA Margin: 16-18% (blended) for FY27. Order Inflow: Targeting consistent >20% growth in pre-sales. Capex/Commissioning: High approval costs for new JDAs to continue; Operating Cash Flow expected to remain negative for next 2 years due to reinvestment in growth pipeline.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total GDV Pipeline: ~INR 42,000 cr. Thane Legacy Land: ~INR 25,000 cr potential (60 acres under development). JDA Pipeline: 7 projects, ~INR 17,000 cr potential (includes Kandivali, Wadala, Sion, Bandra). Recent Launches (Q4): Address by GS (Wadala & Sion) combined GDV INR 6,400 cr; TenX District 9 & Park Street (Thane). Upcoming: Two Mahim projects (launch by Q3 FY27), Kandivali (spillover to FY28).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Two Mahim projects (advanced approval stage) launching in FY27; Kandivali project ramping up; Potential activation of commercial development in Thane (master-planned, timing TBD); Pipeline of negotiated deals spilling into FY27 despite selective discipline in overheated segments.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Targeted micro-market strategy: selective participation in high-demand, supply-constrained MMR micro-markets such as Bandra, Mahim, Sion and Wadala, defined by strong connectivity and proximity to commercial hubs
- Execution excellence as a differentiator: timely delivery and superior construction quality to reinforce trust and long-term brand equity
- Asset-light expansion through the JDA (Joint Development Agreement) model, providing access to premium locations without the capital burden of outright land acquisition, preserving balance sheet strength
- Integrated, end-to-end customer-centric model to enhance conversion, build trust and drive repeat demand
- Premiumisation through brand-led positioning: a three-tier brand architecture (aspirational, premium and luxury) addressing the full spectrum of MMR homebuyers
- Portfolio diversification within MMR across multiple micro-markets to reduce concentration risk and ensure consistent demand visibility
- Manufacturing-style operational discipline in construction execution, applying Lean practices, Six Sigma, Kaizen and OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) principles to de-risk timelines
- Sustainable sourcing policy built on green-first tenders, proximity sourcing (250km rule), resource circularity and digital traceability across Thane and Mumbai project sites
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Raymond Realty's primary development phase centres on its 100-acre owned Thane land bank, with FY26 marking the Company's transition to a scalable, capital-light platform via Joint Development Agreements (JDAs). A marquee project acquisition in Kandivali during Q4 FY26 added to the Gross Development Value (GDV) pipeline, taking the total portfolio to approximately Rs 42,000 crore+, comprising approximately Rs 25,000 crore in the Thane land bank and approximately Rs 17,000 crore across seven JDA projects. During the year the Company launched seven projects across four MMR micro-markets (Thane, BKC, Wadala and Sion), and management states it secures prime JDAs through its MMR brand strength, a track record of early project delivery, and institutional financial discipline that landowners trust.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's real estate sector market size is approximately Rs 22.5 trillion, contributing 7.2% to GDP, with primary residential real estate accounting for nearly two-thirds of the market
- Sector expected to continue steady growth marked by increasing institutionalisation and diversification, with residential and commercial demand remaining resilient
- Flight to quality: branded developers with strong delivery track records are consolidating market share at the expense of unorganised players
- Rising disposable incomes are directing a growing share of household wallets towards premium homeownership
- RBI's accommodative stance (repo rate maintained at 5.25%) lowers borrowing costs and reinforces buyer confidence across segments
- MMR remains the largest and most dominant residential market in India; large-scale infrastructure investments (Coastal Road, Mumbai Metro, Atal Setu, Sewri-Worli Connector, Bandra-Worli Sea Link, Eastern Freeway) are enhancing connectivity and expected to reinforce MMR's position as India's most attractive real estate market
- Government initiatives — Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) 2.0, SWAMIH Fund II, Urban Infrastructure Development Fund, National Urban Digital Mission, Land Record Digitisation and Model Tenancy Act reforms — expected to improve affordability, financing access and regulatory efficiency, supporting long-term housing demand
- Union Budget 2026-27 public capex increased to approximately Rs 12.2 lakh crore, expected to accelerate urban development and support long-term growth in organised residential real estate
- JDA portfolio in Mumbai represents a GDV of approximately Rs 17,000 crore across seven strategically located projects in high-demand micro-markets, built over the past two to three years as the next major driver of scale
- Overall project portfolio spans approximately 12,000 planned residential units with approximately 20 million sq. ft. currently under active construction
- During FY2025-26 the Company launched seven projects across four key MMR micro-markets — Thane, BKC, Wadala and Sion — with encouraging customer response

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Raymond Realty Limited is a real estate developer focused on high-growth micro-markets within the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), demerged from Raymond Limited and listed in July 2025, ranked among the top 5 listed developers in MMR.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Raymond Realty is engaged in the construction and development of residential and retail projects across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), using a capital-efficient model combining its owned 100-acre Thane land bank with an asset-light Joint Development Agreement (JDA) model. It caters to individual homebuyers and investors seeking premium residential and commercial/retail properties in MMR micro-markets including Thane, Bandra, BKC, Wadala and Sion.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's real estate sector market size is approximately Rs 22.5 trillion, contributing 7.2% to GDP, with primary residential real estate accounting for nearly two-thirds of the market
- Sector expected to continue steady growth marked by increasing institutionalisation and diversification, with residential and commercial demand remaining resilient
- Flight to quality: branded developers with strong delivery track records are consolidating market share at the expense of unorganised players
- Rising disposable incomes are directing a growing share of household wallets towards premium homeownership
- RBI's accommodative stance (repo rate maintained at 5.25%) lowers borrowing costs and reinforces buyer confidence across segments
- MMR remains the largest and most dominant residential market in India; large-scale infrastructure investments (Coastal Road, Mumbai Metro, Atal Setu, Sewri-Worli Connector, Bandra-Worli Sea Link, Eastern Freeway) are enhancing connectivity and expected to reinforce MMR's position as India's most attractive real estate market
- Government initiatives — Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) 2.0, SWAMIH Fund II, Urban Infrastructure Development Fund, National Urban Digital Mission, Land Record Digitisation and Model Tenancy Act reforms — expected to improve affordability, financing access and regulatory efficiency, supporting long-term housing demand
- Union Budget 2026-27 public capex increased to approximately Rs 12.2 lakh crore, expected to accelerate urban development and support long-term growth in organised residential real estate
- JDA portfolio in Mumbai represents a GDV of approximately Rs 17,000 crore across seven strategically located projects in high-demand micro-markets, built over the past two to three years as the next major driver of scale
- Overall project portfolio spans approximately 12,000 planned residential units with approximately 20 million sq. ft. currently under active construction
- During FY2025-26 the Company launched seven projects across four key MMR micro-markets — Thane, BKC, Wadala and Sion — with encouraging customer response

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Raymond Realty's primary development phase centres on its 100-acre owned Thane land bank, with FY26 marking the Company's transition to a scalable, capital-light platform via Joint Development Agreements (JDAs). A marquee project acquisition in Kandivali during Q4 FY26 added to the Gross Development Value (GDV) pipeline, taking the total portfolio to approximately Rs 42,000 crore+, comprising approximately Rs 25,000 crore in the Thane land bank and approximately Rs 17,000 crore across seven JDA projects. During the year the Company launched seven projects across four MMR micro-markets (Thane, BKC, Wadala and Sion), and management states it secures prime JDAs through its MMR brand strength, a track record of early project delivery, and institutional financial discipline that landowners trust.

- Diversified portfolio across four key MMR micro-markets (Thane, BKC, Wadala, Sion) reducing single-market concentration

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
